February 13, 1945. Morning Translation.

MISCELLANEOUS

MAINICHI

MEETING OF EDUCATION COMMITTEE OF THE JAPANESE
RESIDENTS CORPORATION

At noon yesterday the
Education Committee of the Japanese Residents Corporation
held a meeting in the assembly hall of the Corporation.
Questions regarding the annual promotion of teachers
of the Japanese schools and the engagement of 3 additional
teachers for primary schools and 6 for middle schools
were discussed.

NEWLY APPOINTED JAPANESE CONSULAR POLICE OFFICERS
VISIT VARIOUS CIRCLES

Yesterday Mr. Ueda, newly
appointed chief of the Japanese Consular Police, and
Mr. Aoyanagi, newly appointed officer in charge of the
2nd Section of the Police, paid visits to various circles
for the purpose of making known their appointments.

KOREAN ARRESTED IN TIENTSIN BROUGHT TO SHANGHAI

Acting on the instruction
of the Shanghai Japanese Consular Police, the Consular
Police at Tientsin arrested a Korean named Myung Suk
Won, age 28, on a charge of fraud and brought him
here on February 11 on the S.S. Hoten Maru.

杂项

《每日新闻》

日本居留民团教育委员会会议

昨日中午，日本居留民团教育委员会在该团公会堂举行会议。会议讨论了关于日本学校教师年度晋升的问题，以及为小学增聘3名教师、为中学增聘6名教师的事宜。

新任日本领事馆警察官员拜访各界

昨日，新任日本领事馆警察署长上田（Ueda，音译）先生和新任警察第二科负责人青柳（Aoyanagi，音译）先生拜访了各界人士，以通报其任职情况。

在天津被捕的朝鲜人被带至上海

奉上海日本领事馆警察署指示，天津领事馆警察于2月11日以欺诈罪逮捕了一名名为明硕元（Myung Suk Won，音译）、28岁的朝鲜人，并经由“奉天丸”号轮船将其押解至上海。

Made by D. S. Umemoto. Forwarded by. J.B.Loo D.I.

A law governing the Shanghai Japanese Residents'
Corporation was promulgated by the Japanese Government in
1905 and by virtue of this decree, an order was issued in 1907
by the then Foreign Minister approving the establishment of
the local Japanese Residents' Corporation which was authorized
to function in the International Settlement, in the French
Concession and in Chinese controlled territory, including
Pootung, within a two mile area from the boundaries of the
International Settlement and the French Concession. Rules
for the enforcement of the Corporation Law were put into effect
in the following year and were subsequently revised as occasion
arose.

The Corporation comprises 60 members bi-annually elected
by Japanese ratepayers; this number, however, will be decreased
to 40 persons at the forthcoming polls on February 23 and 24,
1935 in accordance with stipulations contained in the revised
regulations governing the functions of the Corporation enforced
in December 1934.

With the object of promoting the welfare of the Japanese
community, the following enterprises are at present being
undertaken by the Corporation:-

1) Education of Japanese children: For this purpose, four
primary schools, a commercial school for boys, a high school
for girls and a night school for training in business
procedure are being operated.
2) Medical Treatment
3) Cemetery and Crematorium
4) Relief work for destitutes
5) Loans to merchants: With a view to alleviating trade

主题：日本社群针对日本总领事的局势。
制作人：D. S. Umemoto。转呈人：J.B.Loo，督察。

日本政府于1905年颁布了管辖上海日本居留民团的法律，并依据此法令，时任外务大臣于1907年发布命令，批准成立当地日本居留民团，授权其在国际公共租界、法租界以及包括浦东在内的、距国际公共租界和法租界边界两英里范围内的中国管辖区域内运作。次年实施了执行该民团法律的细则，随后根据情况进行了修订。

该民团由日本纳税人每两年选举产生的60名成员组成；然而，根据1934年12月生效的经修订的民团职能规章规定，在即将于1935年2月23日和24日举行的选举中，这一人数将减少至40人。

为了促进日本社群的福利，民团目前正在进行以下事业：

1) 日本儿童教育：为此目的，正在运营四所小学、一所男子商业学校、一所女子高中和一所商务程序夜校。
2) 医疗救治
3) 墓地和火葬场
4) 贫困救济工作
5) 向商人提供贷款：为了缓解贸易

In order to deliberate on matters affecting Japanese
interests and to maintain co-operation with the various local
authorities and public utility companies, a Negotiation Committee
of seven members was appointed in 1933. Mr. T. Ikeda is the
Chairman. Basing their deliberations on matters relating to

Recent activities in this connection are as follows:-

the issue of an educational grant.
2) Proposals to the Municipal Council for an increase in the
number of Japanese employees.
3) Negotiations with the Shanghai Telephone Co. concerning
the increase in telephone charges.
As the Corporation functions under the supervision of the

国际公共租界内的街道工会位于上海及越界筑路区域。这些街道工会大多存在于北区，由日本公众各阶层成员组成，其中大多数为中下层人士。他们被称为“上海在地日本人”（Shanghai-landers），其在日本居留民团中的利益由约20名成员代表。
涉及其利益的事项由该联合会的常务委员会讨论，并采取适当措施以应对不时出现的任何不利局面。
该联合会以前曾参与与各当局谈判，以表达街道工会成员的意见，但在日本总领事石井（Ishii，音译）先生向常务委员会成员发出口头警告后，已停止此类活动。
目前引起该联合会关注的事项如下：
1) 电话费上涨
关于此事，该联合会北部分会在一次会议上通过决议，抗议涨价。最近，电话公司代表、居留民团和本联合会的代表在日本俱乐部举行了一次会议。未达成决定。
2) 越界筑路问题
已向日本总领事提交提案，并请求其按照

The Japanese Residents' Corporation and the Japanese
Amalgamated Association of Street Unions represent different
interests. The attitude of these bodies towards local affairs
consequently differ and are often divergently opposed. However,
there seems to be no danger of these differences giving rise
to serious enmity or preventing co-operation in matters of
mutual interest. Differences are not so likely to become
intense in the future as in the past. Mr. Yasui, who will
probably be the new paid-chairman of the Japanese Residents'
Corporation, is a man of cool disposition and sound judgment.
Mr. Amano, the present Chairman of the Amalgamated Association
of Street Unions, is a man of a conciliatory nature.

In accordance with the instructions of the Deputy
Commissioner, Special Branch, on the attached extract from
the French Police dated January ..., 1936, on the subject of
agitation among the local Japanese community against Mr. Ishii,
Japanese Consul-General, - have to state that no threatening
attitude has been adopted by the Japanese community against
the Consul-General in protest against his adopting an alleged
weak policy towards the Chinese Authorities and the Shanghai
Municipal Council on the outside roads question.
Regarding the threatening letter which is reported to
have been sent to the Consul-General, the Japanese Consular
Police deny that any such mission was received and as no
protection has been provided to this official the information
can be regarded as groundless.
In view of the fact that the outside roads question is
being dealt with by the Consul-General in consultation with
the local Japanese Naval Authorities who are responsible for
the defence of the area under negotiation, it is hardly
believable that Lieutenant-Colonel Kagesa, who holds the
post of Senior Adjutant to the Military Attache to the
Japanese Legation in China, should interfere in any way with
the work of other officials over local affairs and to support
a movement which is alleged to be carried out by disgruntled
members of the Japanese Street Unions against the Consul-General.
Prior to the assumption of office by Mr. Ishii in 1933,
the local Japanese Amalgamated Association of Street Unions,
of which Mr. Y. Hayashi was the Chairman, had been functioning
on behalf of the Japanese residents and in representing the
opinions of the Japanese community had been submitting petitions

关于据报道已发送给总领事的恐吓信，日本领事馆警察否认收到任何此类信件，且由于未为该官员提供保护，该信息可视为毫无根据。
鉴于越界筑路问题正由总领事与当地日本海军当局协商处理，后者负责谈判区域的防务，因此很难相信担任中国驻日本公使馆武官高级副官的影佐（Kagesa，音译）中校会以某种方式干涉其他官员的地方事务工作，并支持据称由不满的日本街道工会成员发起的针对总领手的运动。
在石井先生于1933年上任之前，由林（Y. Hayashi，音译）先生担任主席的当地日本街道工会联合会一直代表日本居民行事，并在代表日本社群意见方面提交请愿书

Translation of extract from French Police Daily
Intelligence Report dated January 24, 1935.

Parag. 23. Agitation in the local Japanese community
(In continuation of our reports dated 15/1/35 -
Part 1, parag. 24, and 17/1/35 - Part 2, Parag.34)

Agitation which is going on in the local Japanese
community against Mr. ISHII, Japanese Consul-General in
Shanghai, who is accused with adopting a weak attitude
towards the Chinese authorities and the S.M.C., seems to
be developing.

The movement seems to be particularly popular among
members of the Japanese Street Unions who fear that the
Consul-General may yield too readily in the matter of
outside roads. It is even reported that Mr. ISHII
received recently a threatening letter to the effect that
drastic steps would be taken against him should he not
modify his policy.

According to information, which is difficult to
verify, this movement of protest is to a certain degree
supported and inspired by Lt.-Colonel KAGESA, Japanese
Military Attache Adjoint in China, residing in Shanghai,
who was appointed to this post in December last.

Remark of D.C.(Special Branch):
* S.S. For discreet inquiry and report. The matter

1935年1月24日法国警察每日情报报告摘录译文。

第23段. 当地日本侨民中的煽动活动
（续我方1935年1月15日报告——第一部分，第24段，以及1935年1月17日报告——第二部分，第34段）

当地日本侨民中针对日本驻上海总领事石井先生（Mr. ISHII）的煽动活动似乎正在发展，石井先生被指责对中国当局及工部局（S.M.C.）采取软弱态度。

该运动在日本路政同业公会成员中似乎尤为盛行，他们担心总领事在外滩道路（outside roads）问题上可能过于轻易让步。甚至有报告称，石井先生最近收到一封威胁信，声称若他不改变政策，将对他采取激烈手段。

据难以核实的情报显示，这一抗议运动在某种程度上得到了居住在上海的日本驻华副武官影佐祯昭中校（Lt.-Colonel KAGESA）的支持和鼓动，他于去年十二月被任命为该职。

特别处助理处长（D.C.）备注：
* 请秘密调查并报告。此事敏感，需谨慎处理。*

梅本警探（D.S. Umemoto）
特别分部 1935年1月25日

Agitation which is going on in the local Japanese 
community against Mr. ISHII, Japanese Consul-General in 
Shanghai, who is accused with adopting a weak attitude 
towards the Chinese authorities and the S.M.C., seems to 
be developing. 

The movement seems to be particularly popular among 
members of the Japanese Street Unions who fear that the 
Consul-General may yield too readily in the matter of 
outside roads. It is ewen reported that Mr. ISHII 
received recently a threatening letter to the effect that 
drastic steps would be taken against him should he not 
modify his policy. 

According to information, which is difficult to 
verify, this movement of protest is to a certain degree 
supported and inspired by Lt.-Colonel KAGESA, Japanese 
Military Attache Adjoint in China, residing in Shanghai, 
who was appointed to this post in December last.
